hits.text:
Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Temperament Spec
Temperament | Responds to | If you are Heroes | If you are a Menace |
Idealist | Help. Refuses bribes. | Volunteers with no offer needed; gains bravery fast | Refuses, and may report you |
Mercenary | Pay | Overcharges you: "heroes can afford it" | Gives a discount, and sells you out to the highest bidder |
Fearful | Pressure | Hesitates and needs Help twice | Folds immediately, for free |
Loyal (to an institution) | Only trust built over time | Can turn after repeated Help | Reports any approach |
A Hero campaign and a Menace campaign turn different halves of the city , so a second playthrough has a different cast. That's the replay value.

hits.section: Prove the rules small, then dress them › Capstone slice (five weeks)
hits.text:
Prove the rules small, then dress them › Capstone slice (five weeks)
Week | Deliverable | Exit check |
1 | Rules proven in the top-down test | Two routes win, and going loud fails at a cost Done |
2 | The rules move into Unity. Handover laid out in the 3D world. | 28 scenarios pass in Unity |
3 | Cell control, contacts, security, rivals, readability pass | First uncoached playtest |
4 | Final fight (both branches), payoff cut, Intel, event log, debrief | New-player test; freeze the rules |
5 | Tuning, fixes, audio cues. No new systems. | Final uncoached gate |
Gate. An uncoached player can state the objective and fail conditions, pick an approach because of something they learned, explain its cash, time and Trail cost, complete a chain, say why they fought police rather than rivals (or the reverse), and read what the next mission inherits.
If the schedule slips, cut in this order: crowd witnesses (crowds stay decorative) → patrol reroute → camera-block variant → the police branch of the final fight (rivals only). Always keep both routes, the one payoff cut, the debrief and the gate test.

Four operatives, four verbs › Scout
Watch · Listen · Mislead. Watch reveals a routine, and a watcher's sight (its cone) and check-in marks: the cones are the Scout's skill. Listen reveals needs and temperament. Can send rivals after false tips.

One lead, clear owners, named handoffs › Decisions (v0.22.0)
Sky: the controls for real time ( briefs/011/play/HOW-TO-PLAY.md and Motive's fight controls) replace "click to select or move, Shift to group, 1–4 operative, E engage, F fire, C call, click a person for the action card" (section 10). Camera rotation is rejected for now: yaw stays 30.
Sky: the HUD is simple and Syndicate-style, built for real time ( briefs/011/ui/round4 v10, round5 , round5/placement ): roster, verb plate, status pill, price chip, at most two icons over a person, the action panel. The dock is a setting; the default dock (left column or corner) and the finish (cab-cluster or deco-console) are still Sky's open pick.
Sky: "every order shows its full price before you commit" stays. In real time it is met by the price chip on hover, the action panel, the run price on ground hover and the going-loud card.
Aster: section 07's "west street" was the top-down test's compass; as built, the police come in by the north street ( contracts/missions/handover/mission.json ), as Motive's proposal reads.

Nothing hand-authored, everything checked
Consequences | The rules, applied to the mission log | Replaying the mission to confirm the same result |
The mission checker: a generated mission ships only if at least 2 quiet routes win · a loud route exists and costs more Trail · every way to fail can actually happen · no single contact is essential · a player who knows everything finishes with at least a minute to spare. An open case counts as 3 Trail.
The risk is sameness. When everyone is generated, it's easy for nobody to be memorable. Watch Dogs: Legion is the cautionary example. The answer is history, not backstory : people become memorable through what the systems record with you (who you helped, who got braver, who sold you out). Generated text is only a light layer on top. Every fact a person carries must change a price or an outcome: a field that no rule reads is rejected, because detailed bios that change nothing (Legion again) are the opposite of memorable.

§07 HANDOVER › the capstone
the capstone (Sky, 2026-10-15: "the guard comes to visit Inez when she calls him because you bribed / pressured her and that's what makes him leave his post"): the call that pulls the guard off his door is Inez, called because the cell helped, paid or pressured her. Her debt is her need (Help clears it); the affair is her secret (Pressure threatens to expose it).
